create.ponder.fluid_pipe_flow.text_1: A line of Fluid Pipes links the containers at its ends, two or as many as you like
create.ponder.fluid_pipe_flow.text_2: Right-clicking a straight piece with a Wrench adds a window to it
create.ponder.fluid_pipe_flow.text_3: A windowed piece stays straight: pipes placed beside it will not join it
create.ponder.fluid_pipe_flow.text_4: A Mechanical Pump driven by rotation makes the fluid travel through the pipes
create.ponder.fluid_pipe_flow.text_5: Right after starting, nothing is taken out of the source yet
create.ponder.fluid_pipe_flow.text_6: As soon as the flow reaches the far end, the contents move over little by little
create.ponder.fluid_pipe_flow.text_7: The pipes only guide the transfer: no fluid is ever stored inside them
create.ponder.fluid_pipe_interaction.tex: Each open end of a pipe network can work with the block placed in front of it
Anything that stores fluid can be emptied or filled this way
A source block right at an open end gets sucked up...
...and an open end facing empty space pours out new sources
A few other blocks, such as cauldrons, can also be drained by pipes directly
create.ponder.encased_fluid_pipe.text_1: Fluid Pipes can be covered with Copper Casing
create.ponder.encased_fluid_pipe.text_2: Besides hiding the pipe, the casing fixes its openings exactly as they are
create.ponder.encased_fluid_pipe.text_3: A pipe placed next to it no longer makes it open a new side...
create.ponder.encased_fluid_pipe.text_4: ...and removing a neighbour does not close one either
create.ponder.mechanical_pump_flow.text_: A Mechanical Pump decides how fluid moves in the pipes connected to it
The arrow on its body shows which way the fluid is pushed
Everything behind the pump is now being sucked from...
...and everything in front of it receives the fluid
Turning the input the other way does not change the pump direction
To send the fluid the other way, right-click the pump with a Wrench
create.ponder.mechanical_pump_speed.head: Throughput of Mechanical Pumps
create.ponder.mechanical_pump_speed.text: No matter how fast it turns, a pump reaches pipes up to 16 blocks away
With a faster input, the flow spreads through the pipes sooner...
Several pumps on the same network add up their throughput
They must all point the same way, though
create.ponder.valve_pipe.text_1: A Fluid Valve can stop or release the flow inside a pipe line
create.ponder.valve_pipe.text_2: Whether it lets fluid pass depends on the rotation given to its shaft
create.ponder.valve_pipe.text_3: Turned in the opening direction, the valve opens and the fluid flows on
create.ponder.valve_pipe.text_4: Turning it the other way shuts it again
create.ponder.smart_pipe.header: Controlling Fluid flow using Smart Pipes
create.ponder.smart_pipe.text_1: Smart Fluid Pipes let fluids through depending on what kind they are
create.ponder.smart_pipe.text_2: Right next to a source, they choose which fluid gets pulled out of it
create.ponder.smart_pipe.text_3: Right-click the filter slot with something that holds the wanted fluid
create.ponder.smart_pipe.text_4: Placed further along the line, a smart pipe only allows matching fluids to continue
create.ponder.fluid_tank_storage.text_1: Fluid Tanks hold large quantities of fluid
create.ponder.fluid_tank_storage.text_2: Pipes may fill or empty them through any of their faces
create.ponder.fluid_tank_storage.text_3: A Comparator reads how full the tank is
create.ponder.fluid_tank_storage.text_4: In Survival Mode, buckets cannot be poured into or filled from a tank by hand
create.ponder.fluid_tank_storage.text_5: To move fluid in or out of items, use Basins, Item Drains or Spouts
create.ponder.fluid_tank_sizes.text_1: Tanks placed together merge into one larger tank with more room
create.ponder.fluid_tank_sizes.text_2: The footprint of a tank can be as wide as 3 by 3 blocks...
create.ponder.fluid_tank_sizes.text_3: ...while its height can stack up past 30 layers
create.ponder.fluid_tank_sizes.text_4: Right-click with a Wrench to switch the window of a tank on or off
create.ponder.creative_fluid_tank.text_1: A Creative Fluid Tank is an endless source of one fluid
create.ponder.creative_fluid_tank.text_2: Right-click it with an item holding a fluid to pick which one it supplies
create.ponder.creative_fluid_tank.text_3: Pipes can draw that fluid from it for ever, it never runs dry
create.ponder.creative_fluid_tank.text_4: Whatever is pumped back into it simply disappears
create.ponder.hose_pulley.header: Source Filling and Draining using Hose Pulleys
create.ponder.hose_pulley.text_1: A Hose Pulley can fill up or empty out large bodies of fluid
create.ponder.hose_pulley.text_2: Rotation fed into it lowers its hose to the wanted depth
create.ponder.hose_pulley.text_3: With the rotation reversed, the hose is wound back up
create.ponder.hose_pulley.text_4: Pipes attach to the side opposite its front
create.ponder.hose_pulley.text_5: The pipe network can feed fluid into the hose, raising the pool...
create.ponder.hose_pulley.text_6: ...or take fluid out of it, emptying the pool instead
create.ponder.hose_pulley.text_7: How quickly the pulley fills or drains depends only on what the pipe network can move
create.ponder.hose_pulley_level.header: Fill and Drain level of Hose Pulleys
create.ponder.hose_pulley_level.text_1: As long as its hose is fully wound up, the Hose Pulley does nothing
create.ponder.hose_pulley_level.text_2: Draining takes away the uppermost layer first
create.ponder.hose_pulley_level.text_3: It stops once the surface sits one layer below the end of the hose
create.ponder.hose_pulley_level.text_4: Filling starts at the bottom and works its way up
create.ponder.hose_pulley_level.text_5: The pool never rises higher than one layer above the hose end
create.ponder.hose_pulley_infinite.heade: Passively Filling and Draining large bodies of Fluid
create.ponder.hose_pulley_infinite.text_: Lower the hose into a big enough body of water, like an ocean...
...and it hands out or takes in fluid while the water stays exactly as it was
Pipe networks can pull from or push into such a pulley without limit
create.ponder.spout_filling.text_1: A Spout pours fluid into items that are put underneath it
create.ponder.spout_filling.text_2: You cannot pour fluid into a Spout or take any out by hand
create.ponder.spout_filling.text_4: Items to be filled can sit on a Depot placed below the Spout
create.ponder.spout_filling.text_5: When the items arrive on a belt...
create.ponder.spout_filling.text_6: ...the Spout stops each one, fills it and lets it move on by itself
create.ponder.item_drain.header: Emptying Fluid Containers using Item Drains
create.ponder.item_drain.text_1: Item Drains pull the fluid out of items
create.ponder.item_drain.text_2: Right-click it to tip the fluid of the item in your hand into it
create.ponder.item_drain.text_3: Items pushed in from a side...
create.ponder.item_drain.text_4: ...roll over it and leave their fluid behind on the way
create.ponder.item_drain.text_5: Pipes can then draw the collected fluid out of the drain
create.ponder.portable_fluid_interface.t: Pipes have no way to reach the Fluid Tanks of a moving contraption
This interface lets you reach them, and the contraption need not be stopped for it
Put a second one where the first will pass, leaving a gap of 1 or 2 blocks
When one passes the other, the two link up
While linked, the fixed interface stands for every tank on the contraption
Fluid can be pumped into it...
...or pumped back out of the contraption
Once nothing has been moved for a little while, the contraption carries on
create.ponder.pulse_extender.text_1: A Pulse Extender makes a signal that runs through it last longer
create.ponder.pulse_extender.text_2: It turns on shortly after receiving the signal...
create.ponder.pulse_extender.text_3: ...and only turns off again once the set time has run out
create.ponder.pulse_extender.text_4: Scroll on the value panel to choose how long the output is held
create.ponder.pulse_extender.text_5: The time can be set anywhere up to a full hour
create.ponder.pulse_repeater.text_1: After a delay, a Pulse Repeater sends out one brief pulse
create.ponder.pulse_repeater.text_2: The delay before the pulse is set by scrolling on the value panel
create.ponder.pulse_repeater.text_3: Delays as long as one hour are possible
create.ponder.powered_latch.header: Controlling signals using the Powered Latch
create.ponder.powered_latch.text_1: A Powered Latch works like a lever that redstone can flip
create.ponder.powered_latch.text_2: A signal reaching its back turns it on, and it stays on
create.ponder.powered_latch.text_3: A signal coming from the side turns it off again
create.ponder.powered_latch.text_4: You can also flip it yourself with a right-click
create.ponder.powered_toggle_latch.heade: Controlling signals using the Powered Toggle Latch
create.ponder.powered_toggle_latch.text_: A Powered Toggle Latch is a lever that redstone can flip
Each signal arriving at its back switches it to the other state...
...so it goes on, then off with the next one
A right-click toggles it by hand as well
create.ponder.analog_lever.header: Controlling signals using the Analog Lever
create.ponder.analog_lever.text_1: Analog Levers give out an exact amount of redstone power from a single block
create.ponder.analog_lever.text_2: Each right-click raises its output strength by one
create.ponder.analog_lever.text_3: Sneak while right-clicking to lower it step by step
create.ponder.nixie_tube.text_1: Given a redstone signal, Nixie Tubes show its strength as a number
create.ponder.nixie_tube.text_2: Right-click with a written Clipboard to show your own text on them
create.ponder.nixie_tube.text_3: Right-click with a Dye to give the tubes a different glow colour
create.ponder.redstone_link.text_1: Redstone Links carry redstone signals without any wires
create.ponder.redstone_link.text_2: Sneak and right-click one to switch it into receiving mode
create.ponder.redstone_link.text_3: Right-clicking with a Wrench switches it the same way
create.ponder.redstone_link.text_4: Receivers give out the same power as any transmitter up to 256 blocks away
create.ponder.redstone_link.text_5: Items put into its two slots set the frequency it uses
create.ponder.redstone_link.text_6: Links only talk to each other when their frequencies are the same
create.ponder.rose_quartz_lamp.text_1: A Rose Quartz Lamp lights up when it gets a redstone signal
create.ponder.rose_quartz_lamp.text_2: Even after the signal is gone, it keeps putting out redstone power
create.ponder.rose_quartz_lamp.text_3: Lamps placed side by side form a group...
create.ponder.rose_quartz_lamp.text_4: ...and turning one of them on moves the signal there, switching the rest off
create.ponder.rose_quartz_lamp.text_5: A Comparator measures how far away the lit lamp of the group is
create.ponder.rose_quartz_lamp.text_6: A Wrench can also switch a lamp on or off by hand
create.ponder.pulse_timer.header: Redstone output of the Pulse Timer
create.ponder.pulse_timer.text_1: Pulse Timers keep sending out brief pulses, one after another
create.ponder.pulse_timer.text_2: Scroll on the value panel to change the time between pulses
create.ponder.pulse_timer.text_3: Powering its input side pauses the timer and starts its count over
create.ponder.pulse_timer.text_4: Right-click the base of the circuit to flip its output
create.ponder.pulse_timer.text_5: That is handy for machines that only run while they are not powered
